price.title: Electricity Price
price.intro: The current electricity price is exposed as a device value (tile, Insights, flow token). Choose the tariff model:
price.dualWindowIntro: High-tariff time window per weekday (HH:MM). Outside the window the low tariff applies. A day with no times = low tariff all day. A window across midnight (e.g. 22:00–06:00) is allowed.

variable.setup: Setup: An external app (e.g. Tibber, EPEX spot, dynamic tariff) sets the current price via the flow action "EMS: set electricity price (per kWh)". The last value set is used as the current price. Can your price source instead provide a full day-ahead hourly forecast (e.g. "Power by the Hour")? Then use "Price forecast (day-ahead)" below instead — no separate flow needed for the current price.

forecast.info: The current price is read directly from the hourly forecast below — no separate "current price" flow needed. This also powers EV charging for chargers set to "Solar & cheapest hours (forecast)".

forecastSection.title: 📈 Price forecast
forecastSection.desc: This hourly forecast is fed via the "Set price forecast" flow action. Works directly with Power by the Hour's "New prices received" trigger (its Prices token), Tibber, or any similar day-ahead price app. Used by EV chargers set to "Solar & cheapest hours (forecast)" to charge during the cheapest hours before a car's deadline.

price.feedInHint: What you are paid per exported kWh. Leave empty if you do not know — solar a charging car takes is then left unpriced, as before. Entering it makes charge sessions count that solar at the revenue you gave up instead of as free.
price.zonesIntro: For tariffs with more than two periods — standard, peak, night, and a cheap window for EV charging, for example. Every hour not covered by a zone costs the standard rate. A window across midnight (23:00–08:00) is allowed, and a window inside another one wins: that is how a cheap EV hour inside the night rate is expressed.
price.zonesEmpty: No zones yet — everything costs the standard rate.
price.zonesUse: This schedule also drives battery grid-charging in the cheapest hours, the reserve for the most expensive ones, and price-based EV charging.

exportLimit.title: 📤 Export Limit Coordinator
exportLimit.subtitle: automatic

enable.title: Limit inverter feed-in automatically
enable.desc: The EMS fires the inverter's Enable export limit and Disable export limit flows on its own, based on the rules you pick below. Enable to choose the rules and review the setup instructions.

batFull.title: When the home battery is full
batFull.desc: Only useful with a home battery. Without one, leave this off and use one of the rules below.

exportLimit.whenToLimit: When should the inverter be limited?
exportLimit.needFlows: Create the Enable / Disable export limit flows first — see the note below.
exportLimit.needBattery: Configure a home battery under "Home Batteries" first.
exportLimit.needVariablePrice: Requires the "Price forecast" or "Variable" price mode — a fixed or dual tariff never goes negative.

negPrice.title: Limit when the electricity price is negative
negPrice.desc: While feeding in costs money instead of earning it, the limit is applied — with or without a battery. Uses the price from the Electricity Price section. Released again as soon as the price rises above the threshold.

exportLimit.priceThresholdHint: Per kWh. 0 = only at genuinely negative prices.

zero.title: Never feed in (zero export)
zero.desc: Holds the limit permanently, independent of export, price and battery — the two rules above then no longer apply. Use this if your grid operator prohibits feed-in. Surplus that nothing in the house can take is lost.

exportLimit.setupHint: Setup: In the Inverter section above, click ✓ Create / Update Flows to generate the Enable export limit and Disable export limit flows. The coordinator fires those flows automatically — no additional Homey flow needed.

tick.title: Control loop interval
tick.desc: How often the EMS reads its meters and decides. Shorter reacts sooner but reads the inverter, meter and battery correspondingly more often; longer eases the load, and the battery floor and grid-import ceiling take longer to bite. Electricity price, car state of charge and solar forecast do not depend on the interval — each follows its own rhythm, the Solcast fetch for instance at most every 3 hours. Leave at 15 seconds unless the diagnostics below give you a reason.

flowSetup.oneStartOneStop: One Start and one Stop flow per device. More than one flow per trigger will result in duplicate commands.
flowSetup.oneStartOneStopHp: One Start and one Stop flow per heat pump. More than one flow per trigger will result in duplicate commands.
flowSetup.noFlowsFound: No flows found — use "Create / Update Flows" below.
flowSetup.noHeatPumpFlowsFound: No heat pump flows found — use "Create / Update Flows" below.
flowSetup.createNote: Creates two flows in "_Huawei EMS": one to start, one to stop. Re-running overwrites existing flows.
flowSetup.createNoteHp: Creates two flows in "_Huawei EMS": one to start, one to stop the heat pump. Re-running overwrites existing flows.
flowSetup.howBoiler: How it works: The EMS fires two separate triggers: "EMS: start boiler" (solar surplus available) and "EMS: stop boiler" (battery priority or no surplus). Create one Flow per trigger and add the appropriate action.
flowSetup.howPool: How it works: The EMS fires two separate triggers: "EMS: start pool" (solar surplus available) and "EMS: stop pool" (battery priority or no surplus). Create one Flow per trigger and add the appropriate action.
flowSetup.howDehumidifier: How it works: The EMS fires two separate triggers: "EMS: start dehumidifier" (solar surplus available) and "EMS: stop dehumidifier" (battery priority or no surplus). Create one Flow per trigger and add the appropriate action.
flowSetup.howAircon: The EMS fires "EMS wants to start / stop air conditioner" with the device id. Pick the action cards that switch your air conditioner and the flows are created for you.
flowSetup.howHeatPump: How it works: The EMS fires two separate triggers: "EMS: start heat pump" (off-peak or solar surplus) and "EMS: stop heat pump" (battery priority or no surplus). Create one Flow per trigger and add the appropriate action.
flowSetup.howCharger:
How it works: The EMS fires the trigger "EMS: set charger current" on the EMS device on every change. Create a Homey Flow with this trigger and add your charger action.

Available tokens: phase1 phase2 phase3 amps charger_device_id

When amps = 0 → stop charging (e.g. turn off charger).
flowSetup.chargerFlowsHint: 1–2 flows are created per charger, each with its own trigger: "EMS wants to set current" and optionally "EMS wants to start charging". More than one flow per trigger and charger will result in duplicate commands.
flowSetup.noChargerFlowsFound: No flows with trigger "EMS: set charger current" found.

flowSetup.advancedFlows: Advanced flows (check manually if trigger is configured):
flowSetup.createNoteCharger: Automatically creates a Flow in a "_Huawei EMS" folder. Re-running overwrites the existing flow.
flowSetup.flowBStartCharging: Flow B — Start charging (only when idle):
flowSetup.triggerUnknown: Trigger unknown for this flow — reload flows
flowSetup.fireTitle: Fire "{{card}}" exactly as the EMS would, and report whether any flow was listening
flowSetup.firedUnheardHint: The card fired, but no flow is built on it — nothing ran. Give the flow a trigger, or check you are looking at the right card.
flowSetup.placeholderTriggerHint: This flow still has its placeholder trigger. The EMS never fires that card, so the flow will not run until you replace the trigger in Homey.
flowSetup.howBattery:
How it works: Each row creates one Homey Flow in "_Huawei EMS". Select the matching Luna2000 action card from the dropdown.

Force Charge, Normal Mode and Max Discharge Power already come with a working trigger — the EMS fires them itself once price-based charging is enabled for this battery. Leave those alone: that flow is how the EMS reaches your battery, and replacing the trigger switches price control off. The other rows get a placeholder trigger for you to replace in Homey (e.g. energy price, time schedule, EMS: battery is full).

Example: WHEN Tibber price > 0.30 CHF → THEN Force Discharge 3000 W down to 20% SOC

Note: pressing the button again deletes these flows by name and creates them anew — a trigger you changed by hand is lost.
flowSetup.noFlowsCreateBelow: No flows found — create them below.
flowSetup.createNoteBattery: Automatically creates Flows in a "_Huawei EMS" folder. Re-running overwrites the existing flows.
flowSetup.flowsCreatedSetTrigger: Flow(s) created in "_Huawei EMS" — the placeholder ones still need a trigger in Homey
flowSetup.howInverter:
How it works: Each row below creates one Homey Flow in "_Huawei EMS". Select the matching action card from your installed apps on the right.

Enable export limit and Disable export limit already come with a working trigger — the EMS fires them itself when the export-limit coordinator switches, so leave those alone. The three limit rows get a placeholder trigger for you to replace in Homey (e.g. a price app).

Example: WHEN Tibber price > 0.30 CHF → THEN Set max feed-in power to 0 W

Note: pressing the button again deletes these flows by name and creates them anew — a trigger you changed by hand is lost.
flowSetup.howCar: How it works: Pick your vehicle's "set charge limit" action and two target values (e.g. 80% everyday, 100% before a trip). Create the flows and two flows are added to "_Huawei EMS": WHEN "EMS: set car target charge" (this car, that %) THEN your vehicle action at the fixed %. The EMS fires the trigger when you call the flow action "EMS: set car target charge (%)" (soc = 80 or 100).
flowSetup.noCarFlowsYet: No flows yet — use "Create charge flows" below.
flowSetup.createNoteCar: Pick the vehicle action for each target. One flow is created per selected target in "_Huawei EMS": THEN the chosen action. Re-running overwrites them.

priceFlowSetup.how: How it works: pick the device that publishes hourly prices (e.g. your Power by the Hour station) and its trigger card below. The EMS creates one flow for this_day, pre-wired to the "Set price forecast" action. One manual step remains: open the created flow and drag the Prices token from the trigger into the action's "Prices" field — Homey doesn't let apps do this token wiring automatically.
priceFlowSetup.nextHoursWarn: ⚠ Don't create a next_hours flow with the same Prices token. this_day and tomorrow both anchor the array to a fixed midnight boundary — safe to combine, and normally enough for a full 2-day view. next_hours anchors it to the current hour instead; if your source (e.g. Power by the Hour) always sends the full day's prices from midnight, feeding that same token into a next_hours flow shifts every price by however many hours have passed since midnight, silently corrupting the data. If you already created one like this, delete it in Homey (or empty its action).
priceFlowSetup.cardTip: Which trigger card? Pick the one that fires once with the whole batch of upcoming hourly prices — its token list (shown below the dropdown) should contain something like Prices holding a full list, not a single number. Do not pick a card that fires every hour with just the current price (e.g. "Price changed" / "Prijs update") — that only gives one value, not a forecast. For Power by the Hour this is usually called "New prices received" / "Nieuwe prijzen ontvangen" / "Neue Preise erhalten" — marked ★ below when found on the selected device.
priceFlowSetup.dragTokenHint: drag the price-array token into the action's matching field after creating the flows.
priceFlowSetup.selectDeviceAndCard: Select a device and trigger card first
priceFlowSetup.emsDeviceNotResolved: EMS device not resolved yet — try again in a moment
priceFlowSetup.selectAtLeastOnePeriod: Select at least one period (This day / Tomorrow)

priceFlowSetup.createdDragToken: flow(s) created in "_Huawei EMS" — open each and drag the price token in.

carRow.readyByHint: Battery capacity and "Ready by" are used by chargers in "Solar & cheapest hours (forecast)" mode to plan cheap-price charging before this time. Leave "Ready by" blank to disable deadline planning for this car.
carRow.liveReadingTitle: Current live reading from this capability
carRow.noCapabilitySelected: The vehicle reports no target, so the EMS uses the number above. Leave it empty and the car is charged without a limit. The flow action "EMS: set car target charge" overrides it until the next time this page is saved.

simpleRow.surplusHint: W — minimum solar surplus required to turn on
simpleRow.sustainHint: sec — start delay (surplus must hold for this long before turning on)
simpleRow.graceHint: sec — stop delay (device keeps running this long after surplus drops)
simpleRow.startupGraceHint: sec — reaction grace — after a start, wait this long for power; after an EMS stop, allow this long before "still on" counts as switched on externally
simpleRow.maxRunHint: min — max. run time (when set, device runs for this duration and only stops when time is up; 0 = run while surplus available)
simpleRow.cooldownHint: min — restart cooldown after automatic stop (prevents short-cycling)
simpleRow.minPowerHint: W — "still running" threshold: below this the cycle counts as finished (0 = off)
simpleRow.surplusHintTitle: Minimum solar surplus to turn on (W)
simpleRow.sustainHintTitle: Surplus must hold for this many seconds before EMS turns it on (0 = start immediately)
simpleRow.graceHintTitle: Surplus may drop for this many seconds before EMS turns it off (0 = stop immediately)
simpleRow.startupGraceHintTitle: The device's actuation and reporting lag, used on both sides: after an EMS start, wait this long for power before a below-threshold reading counts as an external OFF (power-based state only); after an EMS stop, a device still reading "on" within this time is treated as slow rather than as switched on by the user. Raise it for devices whose app reports slowly (e.g. cloud-connected air conditioners).
simpleRow.maxRunHintTitle: When set, device runs for exactly this duration and ignores surplus drops during that time (0 = run while surplus is available)
simpleRow.cooldownHintTitle: Minimum minutes before EMS may restart after a power-drop stop (0 = no limit)
simpleRow.minPowerHintTitle: While running: stop if measured power drops below this value (0 = disabled; requires Power (W) capability)

stateSrcHint.onoff: Reads the device on/off switch — the normal case.
stateSrcHint.power: Reads on/off from measured power (needs a Power capability) — for always-on plugs where start/stop toggle an internal load (pool heater/filter).
stateSrcHint.ems: The EMS trusts its own start/stop bookkeeping and never adopts the device state — for devices nudged via setpoints/hysteresis (e.g. a heat pump), where neither the switch nor the power reflects the EMS command.

modeHint.solar: Only charges when enough solar surplus is available; the power follows the surplus.
modeHint.solarOffpeak: Charges on solar surplus during the day. If the car is not yet at its target when the fixed off-peak time window (set under EV Chargers → Off-Peak Charging, enabled via the Off-Peak toggle on the EMS device tile) starts, it charges at full power during that window — the window is always the same time, not price-aware.
modeHint.solarLowtariff: Charges on solar surplus during the day. Charges at full power whenever the "Low / high tariff" schedule (Electricity Price → Low / high tariff) currently says LOW tariff — reuses that same weekday window instead of a separate Off-Peak schedule.
modeHint.solarPrice: Charges on solar surplus first. What solar won't cover by the car's "Ready by" deadline (set under Cars) is charged during whichever hours are actually cheapest, based on the live price forecast (Electricity Price → Set price forecast flow) — not a fixed window.
modeHint.always: Charges at the maximum possible power as soon as the cable is plugged in — regardless of solar or battery state.

chargers.noPlanYet: No plan yet — check Cars (Ready by / Battery) and the Price forecast under Electricity Price.
chargers.dualNotConfigured: ⚠ Dual tariff not configured — see Electricity Price → Low / high tariff.
chargers.chargingCarHint: optional · used to stop this charger when its car reaches the target SOC
chargers.adjustmentIntervalHint: sec — how long the surplus must hold before the charge current is stepped up (↑) and before it is stepped down (↓). Higher = fewer adjustments. Down at 0 reduces at once, as it always did; raise it if a home battery can bridge a passing cloud, so the charger does not drop a rung it has to climb back a minute later. Sustained grid import overrides the down delay after 60 s. After any step down, 5 min pass before it may rise again.
chargers.phasesTitle: Number of phases this charger uses
chargers.autoPhaseSwitchTitle: Auto phase-switching: below 4140 W (6A × 3ph) the EMS uses 1-phase charging; at or above it switches to 3-phase

pvForecast.title: Solar Forecast (Solcast)
pvForecast.resourceIdPlaceholder:
One per line (or comma-separated) — e.g.
abcd-1234-ef56-7890
9876-5432-dcba-0fed
pvForecast.desc: Free Hobbyist account at Solcast Toolkit — register your PV system with its exact details, then copy your API key (under Your name → Your API key) and Resource ID (click your site on the map). Multiple sites (e.g. north + south roof) — enter one per line; their forecasts are summed. New accounts get 10 API calls/day (older accounts 50) and each site is one call, so the app spaces fetches out automatically to stay within budget (≈ 8 calls/day total whether 1 or several sites) and caches across restarts — no flows needed. Result appears under Diagnostics → EMS Diagnostics.
pvForecast.chartAlt: Forecast PV output over the coming day
pvForecast.chartOff: Forecast is switched off in the saved settings
pvForecast.chartUnconfigured: No API key or site ID saved yet

evChargers.title: EV Chargers
evChargers.subtitle: solar surplus & tariff

compare.intro: Three modes below use grid power outside solar surplus — each solves it differently:

offpeak.name: Off-peak window
offpeak.when: When: fixed daily time window, same every day

lowtariff.name: Low tariff
lowtariff.when: When: whenever your Low/High weekday schedule says LOW

cheapest.name: Cheapest hours (forecast)
cheapest.when: When: dynamically — the actual cheapest hours, per real price data
cheapest.setup: Setup: Electricity Price → Price forecast + Cars → Ready by

compare.ruleOfThumb: Rule of thumb: have real hourly price data (e.g. Power by the Hour, Tibber)? Use Cheapest hours — it's the most accurate. Only a fixed cheap/expensive schedule, no live prices? Use Off-peak window or Low tariff depending on which schedule you already maintain.

solarFirst.title: Solar surplus priority
solarFirst.desc: During the off-peak window: if solar surplus is available, the EMS uses it instead of the grid. Disable to always charge at the configured off-peak limit during the window, regardless of solar.

offpeak.title: Off-Peak Charging
offpeak.toggleHint: Enable/disable using the Off-Peak toggle on the EMS device tile in Homey.
offpeak.chargeLimitHint: Per charger · applies to both days

weekendDiffers.title: Different window on weekends
weekendDiffers.desc: Set separate start and end times for EV charging on Saturday and Sunday.

evChargers.rowEnabledHint: When off, the EMS leaves this device alone entirely — it is neither started nor stopped.

cars.title: Cars
cars.subtitle: electric or hybrid
cars.intro: Add one or more vehicles. Per car, the current charge level (read from the selected device) and the target charge (set via flow) are exposed as their own device values (tile, Insights, flow tokens). Use each car's Flow setup to apply the target charge to the vehicle.

heatPumps.title: Heat Pumps
heatPumps.hint: Add each heat pump you want EMS to control. Set the minimum solar surplus required to start it, and optionally a start delay (surplus must hold that many seconds before EMS turns it on) and a stop delay (surplus may drop for that many seconds before EMS turns it off — avoids short cycling).

boilers.title: Boilers / Immersion Heaters
boilers.hint: Add each boiler or immersion heater you want EMS to control. Set the minimum solar surplus required to turn it on, and optionally a start delay and a stop delay to prevent rapid switching.

pool.title: Pool / Whirlpool
pool.hint: Add your pool or whirlpool pump. EMS will run it whenever sufficient solar surplus is available. Use the start and stop delays to avoid short on/off cycles.

dehumidifier.title: Dehumidifier
dehumidifier.hint: Add your dehumidifier. EMS will run it whenever sufficient solar surplus is available. Use the start and stop delays to avoid short on/off cycles.

aircon.title: Air Conditioner
aircon.hint: Add your air conditioner. EMS will run it whenever sufficient solar surplus is available. Use the start and stop flows to switch it.

inverter.title: Solar Inverter
inverter.subtitle: solar production source
inverter.desc: The EMS reads solar production (W) from this device to calculate available surplus. Multiple inverters are summed.

houseMeter.title: House Consumption Meter
houseMeter.subtitle: Optional. Shows house consumption on the device tile. Without it, house load is derived from solar, grid and battery readings.
houseMeter.desc: Optional. Used to show house consumption in the device tile. If omitted, house load is derived from solar, grid, and battery readings.

homeBatteries.title: Home Batteries
homeBatteries.subtitle: Optional but recommended. Supplies the battery SOC used for battery protection: below the minimum the EMS stops surplus devices and throttles charging.
homeBatteries.desc: Optional but recommended. The EMS uses battery SOC to protect the battery — when SOC falls below the minimum, surplus devices are stopped and EV charging is throttled or paused.

socZones.title: Battery: surplus split
socZones.orangeBudgetHint:
Extra power devices may draw from
the battery while in the reserve zone
socZones.legendDesc: Green (above Normal SOC): all devices run on full solar budget. Orange (Reserve → Normal SOC): devices start in priority order if their minimum surplus ≤ current export + Orange Budget. The budget is shared — each started device reduces what remains for the next. Red (below Reserve SOC): all devices stop — battery charges at full speed. Set Reserve SOC to 0 to use only red and green.

shareRamp.hint: The house is served from the same production, so a high share at high house load can draw from the grid.
shareRamp.chartAlt: Share of PV production released to devices, by battery level
shareRamp.stopNote: below that: every device off, battery charges at full power

forecastGate.title: 🌤 Solar-forecast start gate
forecastGate.desc: On a day with a poor forecast, starts are held back — heat pump / boiler / pool / dehumidifier / air conditioning, and solar EV charging too — so the battery keeps enough charge for the night. Anything already running finishes normally, including a charge in progress. Charging you asked for explicitly (instant, always, off-peak, price, low tariff) is never held back. Requires an active Solcast forecast; falls back to normal operation when the forecast is missing or stale.
forecastGate.adaptiveHint: Blocks starts when today's remaining forecast can't refill the battery to 100 % (uses capacity + current SOC).
forecastGate.compareBlocked: {have} kWh forecast left today, {need} kWh needed
forecastGate.compareOpen: {have} kWh forecast left today covers the {need} kWh needed
forecastGate.compareHysteresis: {have} kWh forecast left today — reopens from {reopen} kWh (hysteresis)
forecastGate.whyStale: no fresh Solcast forecast, so normal operation
forecastGate.whyNoCapacity: adaptive mode needs the battery capacity to be filled in

homeBatteries.priceHint: Charges from the grid in the cheapest hours (looking ahead 24h — no fixed deadline, so it can wait for a genuinely cheaper hour) to reach Target SOC. Outside the reserved priciest hours, discharge is held back so the battery has capacity when it matters most. Wire this up below in Flow setup: "Force Charge" (charging), "Max Discharge Power" set to ~0 (reserve/hold), and "Normal Mode" (default).

emsInfo.summary: How does the EMS work? — Setup & Flow-based control
emsInfo.whatBody: The EMS monitors solar surplus, battery SOC, and grid power every 15 seconds and automatically controls EV chargers, heat pumps, boilers, pool pumps, and dehumidifiers — maximising self-consumption without draining the battery below the configured minimum or pulling power from the grid. An optional Solcast solar forecast lets it hold off starting devices on a poor-forecast day to protect the battery for the evening.
emsInfo.step1Body: Click ↻ Reload devices (top right). The EMS reads all Homey devices. Then use the dropdowns below to assign the correct devices and capabilities to each role.
emsInfo.secInverter: Inverter — Measures PV production (W). Multiple devices are summed.
emsInfo.secMeter: Power Meter (P1) — Grid connection meter: positive = import, negative = export. Used as the basis for all control decisions.
emsInfo.secHouse: House Consumption — Optional: direct house load meter. If omitted, the EMS calculates consumption from the energy balance (PV − Grid − Battery).
emsInfo.secBattery: Home Batteries — Assign the SOC capability and the usable capacity (kWh). Under Surplus split, set two battery levels each with a percentage: the fuller the battery, the larger the share of PV production the devices may claim, rising evenly between the two. Below the lower level every device stops and the battery charges at full power. Use Flow Actions to create flows that force-charge, force-discharge, or limit the battery’s charge/discharge power via Homey Flows. The export limit coordinator in the inverter section can fire flows when the battery is full, when the electricity price is negative, or permanently (zero export).
emsInfo.secSolcast: Solar Forecast (Solcast) — Optional. Enter a free Solcast Hobbyist Resource ID + API key to get a PV forecast (today/tomorrow, up to 7 days ahead; multiple sites, e.g. east + west roof, are summed). Shown in Diagnostics → EMS Diagnostics and available as flow triggers/conditions. The Solar-forecast start gate (under Home Batteries) can hold off starting devices on a poor-forecast day, manually (kWh threshold) or adaptively (based on battery capacity + SOC).
emsInfo.secChargers: EV Chargers — Continuous current control 6–32 A (1- or 3-phase, with automatic phase switching if supported). A built-in filter prevents rapid current ramping. Flows must be linked in Homey to set the charge current. Optionally assign a car per charger to track its SOC and set a target charge level.
emsInfo.secHeatPumps: Heat Pumps — On/off control via Flow. Configurable minimum surplus threshold. Measured power (W) is used to avoid rapid on/off switching.
emsInfo.secOthers: Boilers / Pools / Dehumidifiers / Air conditioners — Same logic as heat pumps, each with its own Start/Stop flow cards.
emsInfo.secPriority: Priority order — Configure which device gets surplus first: e.g. EV charger → heat pump → boiler → pool → dehumidifier. Lower-priority devices only receive what remains.
emsInfo.step3Intro: The EMS decides when a device runs but never sends direct device commands — instead it fires Flow trigger cards that you link to your devices in Homey:
emsInfo.flowEvCurrent:
EV — Set charge current
Trigger "EMS wants to set charger current" → tokens amps, phase1/2/3, charger_device_id. Action: charger app "Set current".
emsInfo.flowEvStart:
EV — Start charging
Trigger "EMS wants to start charging" — fired once when charging activates (for charger apps that require an explicit Start command).
emsInfo.flowHeatPump:
Heat pump — Start / Stop
Triggers "EMS wants to start heat pump" / "EMS wants to stop heat pump". Only fired when surplus ≥ minimum threshold.
emsInfo.flowBoiler:
Boiler — Start / Stop
Triggers "EMS wants to start boiler/heater" / "EMS wants to stop boiler/heater".
emsInfo.flowPool:
Pool — Start / Stop
Triggers "EMS wants to start pool pump" / "EMS wants to stop pool pump". On the first tick after app start no flows are fired (observation mode).
emsInfo.flowDehumidifier:
Dehumidifier — Start / Stop
Triggers "EMS wants to start dehumidifier" / "EMS wants to stop dehumidifier" — same solar-surplus logic as heat pumps/boilers/pool.
emsInfo.flowAircon:
Air conditioner — Start / Stop
Triggers "EMS wants to start air conditioner" / "EMS wants to stop air conditioner" — same solar-surplus logic as heat pumps/boilers/pool.
emsInfo.step3Footer: Battery and inverter also have flow triggers (force charge/discharge, max power, export limit) — set them up from the Home Batteries section's Flow Actions.
emsInfo.step4Body: Use the ✓ Create / Update Flows button in each device section — it automatically creates the required flows in the Homey folder "_Huawei EMS". You can then open the Homey app, edit those flows, and link them to your devices.
emsInfo.step5Body: The Diagnostics section below has an EMS Diagnostics panel (live tick health, the last decision, PV forecast, and app memory usage) and an EMS History log of recent mode/device/charger events, with a Copy button for sharing.
emsInfo.offpeakTip: 💡 Tip — Off-peak charging: Enable Offpeak charging on the EMS device in Homey to charge EVs at full power during cheap overnight tariffs when solar surplus is insufficient. Solar surplus still takes priority when available (configurable), and weekday/weekend windows can differ.

gridMeter.title: Grid Meter
gridMeter.subtitle: grid import / export source
gridMeter.desc: The EMS reads grid power from here to determine how much surplus is available. Positive = buying, negative = selling. Multiple meters are summed.

importLimit.title: Grid import limit — whole house (load shedding)
importLimit.desc: A hard safety ceiling on TOTAL grid import (e.g. the site's main fuse rating). It works from the measured import at your grid meters — what the house still draws after solar and battery, not total consumption. Every tick the EMS starts from that reading and reduces or holds back EV charging (Instant / Always-charge / Off-peak / Price / Low-tariff — all tiers that would otherwise draw unconditionally), Home Battery force-charge, and any new heat pump / boiler / pool / dehumidifier / air conditioner start as needed to stay under this limit — EV chargers step down gracefully where possible, the other device types (on/off only) simply have their start denied if it wouldn't fit. Leave at 0 if you don't need a whole-house cap.
